common_name: Vates Kale (Dwarf Blue Curled Scotch Kale)

planting.note: Direct sow or start indoors; also an excellent fall crop, since Vates is especially cold-hardy and its flavor sweetens noticeably after frost.

directions: Direct sow or transplant into fertile, well-drained soil in full sun, spacing plants 12-18 inches apart. Vates is a classic dwarf selection of curly Scotch kale, bred at Virginia's Truck Experiment Station for a compact, low, uniform habit that resists bolting and lodging better than taller curly kales, with tightly ruffled blue-green leaves. It is exceptionally cold-hardy, tolerating hard freezes and actually improving in flavor as cool weather converts starches to sugars, making it a mainstay of fall and winter kale plantings across a wide range of climates. Harvest outer leaves regularly as needed, leaving the growing center intact for continued production over a long harvest season.
